title: Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw

alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Extra Low Interstitials, ASTM F136 / ISO 5832-3) is the medical-grade standard for permanent implantable devices. faq.q: What is a titanium spinal pedicle screw?
faq.a: A titanium spinal pedicle screw is a precision-machined spine fixation component used in polyaxial pedicle screw for spinal fixation. Manufactured from Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What torque should I use for titanium spinal pedicle screw?
faq.a: Recommended installation torque depends on thread size and lubrication. For M5 titanium fasteners: 4-5 Nm (dry), 3-4 Nm (with anti-seize). Always use titanium-compatible anti-seize compound to prevent galling (cold welding) of threads.

faq.q: How is titanium spinal pedicle screw manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw is manufactured using Cold heading. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium spinal pedicle screw?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
